questions.q: Why does a governance committee look at aggregate quality metrics instead of individual rule results?
options: A committee wants a small set of rolled-up numbers, not a list of hundreds of individual rule pass/fail results
Individual rule results are never computed
Aggregate metrics are required by law
Rule-level results are classified information
questions.explain: The lesson explains that committees want aggregate numbers like overall pass rate and critical-rule pass rate, not a raw list of every rule's result.

questions.q: Who should decide which data quality rules count as 'critical' for the critical-rule pass rate?
options: It's a governance decision that should go through the governance workflow, not a call made silently by the dashboard builder
Whoever built the dashboard, without any review
It's fixed permanently by the BI tool vendor
It doesn't matter which rules are critical
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the critical/not-critical decision should go through the governance workflow from Lesson 8, not be made silently.

questions.q: Per the lesson, why are adoption metrics harder to collect than data quality metrics?
options: They require pulling together usage logs, access logs, and manual tracking rather than reading results from one existing rule-results table
Adoption metrics don't actually exist
Adoption is measured only once a year
Adoption metrics require no data at all
questions.explain: Quality results already sit in a table; adoption usually requires combining several different sources by hand.

questions.q: What does the lesson say 'high quality, low adoption' usually indicates?
options: A change-management problem — people haven't noticed or don't trust the governed data yet
The data quality rules are wrong
The program should be shut down immediately
Nothing — this combination can't happen
questions.explain: The lesson frames high quality with low adoption as a trust/awareness gap, not a data problem — addressed in Chapter 4.

questions.q: Which is listed as an example adoption metric in this lesson?
options: Percentage of new reports or dashboards built against approved, governed data sources
Server uptime percentage
Number of office locations
Total company revenue
questions.explain: The lesson lists governed-source usage, steward engagement, and glossary usage as adoption metrics — not infrastructure or financial metrics.
